findings.reason: without teaching `_rederive_waits` the flag (or recording it on the pointer and honouring it there), the node would land a flag whose effect is erased within one sweep, and the test arm that inspects the pointer at dispatch time would stay green while production parks.
findings.text: §31 makes `--waits-only-after` a dispatch-time property of the stored request, but every admission pass rewrites a queued or awaiting request's waits: `advance_waiting_requests` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2083-2106`) calls `_rederive_waits` unconditionally on each candidate, and that function recomputes them through `derive_wait_refs` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1220-1229`), which unions the section's `plan-section-depends-on` refs, the plan's `depends_on`, and the node's `--after` refs; only the `run:`-prefixed refs are preserved (`:2064-2069`). A request dispatched with the flag would therefore have §8's 14 section waits written back on the next pass, before it was ever launched, and park exactly as the section's motivating case describes

findings.reason: two implementers reading §31 and §14 side by side reach different behaviours, and the narrower reading leaves the reported defect partly unrepaired while the done-when's all-four arm can still pass on a fixture whose plan declares no plan-level dependency.
findings.text: the flag is defined by what it drops as "not on its section's `plan-section-depends-on` refs", one of the three inherited sources the plan itself declares: §14 (`plan.html:80`) states a request's waits are "the union of its section's `plan-section-depends-on` refs, its plan's `depends_on`, the gates on its section, and the requests it names with `--after`". A node implementing the exclusion literally keeps the plan-level `depends_on` and the section's gates, so a correction node filed under a section of a plan that carries a plan-level dependency still parks behind it, and the section's own sentence "waits only on the runs and sections its `--after` refs name" ("only") is then false of the code

findings.reason: as written the sentence promises section refs the option cannot carry, inviting a node to add section resolution to `--after` (work §31 does not otherwise require) or to deliver a flag whose description does not match it.
findings.text: §31 says the request "waits only on the runs and sections its `--after` refs name", but `--after` carries request ids alone: the option is `metavar="REQUEST-ID"` with help "Wait for a queued request to land" (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1102-1105`), §14 describes it as `--after <request-id>`, and `derive_wait_refs` prefixes each with `run:` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1228`)

findings.reason: one missing edge serializes them; without it the plan violates its own one-writer-per-file rule and the two nodes' hunks in `queue_admission.py` collide at merge.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` gives §31 `s` refs `s28` and `s29` only, while §25 also writes `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` (its section names that module and its write paths include it) and §25 declares only `s18`; §31's chain reaches `s18` through `s28→s26→s18` and `s29→s18`, so §25 and §31 are ready together and the queue would launch two nodes editing `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` at once
